title: Minimum wages apply to all workers
text: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, the minimum wage notified by the government must be paid to employees. The Code applies to workers in both organised and unorganised sectors, so an employer cannot legally pay you less than the minimum wage for your work and area.
next: Note your wage, hours and employer name. Contact the district labour office, or ask Tele-Law (14454) for free advice.

title: Wages must be paid on time
text: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, monthly wages must be paid before the end of the 7th day of the next month. If your employer keeps delaying or withholding wages, that is a violation and you can claim the unpaid amount.
next: Keep proof of work (messages, attendance, bank entries). Complain to the labour office of your district, or call Tele-Law (14454) for free guidance.

title: Working hours and overtime
text: Under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, a worker cannot be made to work more than eight hours in a day or more than six days in a week. Overtime must be paid at twice the normal rate of wages (also in the Code on Wages, 2019).
next: Write down your daily hours. If overtime is unpaid, raise it with your employer in writing and then with the labour office.

title: Social security for unorganised and gig workers
text: The Code on Social Security, 2020 asks the Central Government to make social security schemes for unorganised workers, and lets it make schemes for gig and platform workers, covering things like life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity benefits and old age protection. Which scheme you get depends on what the government has notified.
next: Ask your employer or platform which schemes apply to you, and check with the labour department for registration.

title: Eviction needs proper process
text: A landlord cannot simply throw a tenant out. Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021, eviction goes through a Rent Authority (appeal to the Rent Court), for reasons such as not paying rent for two months in a row or misusing the property after a written notice. The Model Act applies only where your State has adopted it; otherwise your State's rent law applies.
next: Ask for the notice in writing, keep your rent receipts, and do not sign anything you do not understand. Contact your District Legal Services Authority (15100) for free advice.

title: Security deposit
text: Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021, a security deposit is capped at two months' rent for a home (six months for non-residential premises). A landlord should return it when you vacate after deducting only genuine dues. This applies where your State has adopted the Act; otherwise your State's rent law applies.
next: Take photos when you leave, ask for a written account of deductions, and send a written demand. If still refused, seek legal aid (15100).

text: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 you have the right to complain about defective goods and can seek a repair, replacement, refund and compensation.

title: Where and how to file a consumer complaint
text: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 you can file a complaint with the District Consumer Commission, and it can be filed electronically. You must usually file within two years from the date the problem arose. Smaller claims go to the District Commission; under the 2021 Rules it hears claims up to Rs 50 lakh, the State Commission Rs 50 lakh to Rs 2 crore, and the National Commission above Rs 2 crore. Online filing is through the e-Daakhil portal.
next: Gather bills and messages, send a written complaint to the seller first, then file online or call 1915.

title: Protection from domestic violence
text: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 protects women from domestic violence. The woman, a Protection Officer or anyone on her behalf can apply to the Magistrate (Section 12), and the Magistrate can pass protection orders (Section 18).
next: If you are in danger, call 112 or the women helpline 181. You can also approach a Protection Officer or the magistrate, and get free legal aid (15100).

title: Free legal advice and legal aid
text: Tele-Law gives free pre-litigation legal advice to all citizens through a Common Service Centre, the Tele-Law app, or the helpline 14454. Each case gets about a 20-minute appointment with a panel lawyer and up to 3 consultations. Court costs are not automatically free. For a free lawyer, people in the categories listed under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act (for example women, children, SC/ST and low-income people) can contact the Legal Services Authority (NALSA helpline 15100) and must show proof of their category.
next: Call 14454 or visit your nearest Common Service Centre for advice, or call 15100 for a free lawyer.

(f) An industrial workman; or
(g) In custody, including custody in a protective home within the meaning of clauses
(g) of section 2 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, .1956, or in a juvenile
home within the meaning of clause G) of section 2 of the Juvenile Justice Act,
1986, or in a psychiatric hospital or psychiatric nursing home within the meaning
of clause (g) of section 2 of the Mental Health Act, 1987; or
(h) In receipt of annual income less than rupees nine thousand or such other higher
amount as may be prescribed by the State Government, if the case is before a
court other than the Supreme Court, and less than rupees twelve thousand or
such other higher amount as may be prescribed by the Central Government, if
the case is before the Supreme Court.

13. Entitlement to legal services

(1) Persons who satisfy all or any of the criteria specified in section 12 shall be
entitled to receive legal Services provided that the concerned Authority is satisfied that
such person has a prima facie case to prosecute or to defend.
(2) An affidavit made by a person as to his income may be regarded as sufficient for
making him eligible to the entitlement of legal services under this Act unless the
concerned Authority has reason to disbelieve such affidavit.

FINANCE, ACCOUNTS AND AUDIT
